title: Syringe-injectable Mesh Electronics for Stable Chronic Rodent Electrophysiology
protocol: Thermally evaporate 100 nm of Ni onto a clean Si wafer.
Spin-coat SU-8 2000.5 negative photoresist onto the wafer at 4,000 rpm for an approximate thickness of 400–500 nm.
Soft bake the wafer on a hotplate for 1 min at 65 °C followed by 1 min at 95 °C.
Load the wafer into a mask aligner to expose the SU-8 with PL mask-1.
Expose at an i-line (365 nm wavelength) dose of 100 mJ/cm².
Post bake the wafer on a hotplate for 1 min at 65 °C followed by 1 min at 95 °C.
Immerse the wafer in a tray of SU-8 developer.
Gently agitate the solution for 2 min until the mesh pattern is fully developed.
Rinse the wafer in a tray of isopropyl alcohol for 1 min and blow dry.
Hard bake the wafer on a hotplate at 180 °C for 1 h.
Spin-coat LOR3A onto the wafer at 4000 rpm for an approximate thickness of 300 nm.
Bake the wafer on a hotplate at 180 °C for 5 min.
Spin-coat S1805 positive photoresist at 4000 rpm for an approximate thickness of 500 nm.
Bake the wafer on a hotplate at 115 °C for 1 min.
Load the wafer into a mask aligner to expose the S1805 with PL mask-2 corresponding to the metal interconnects and I/O pads.
Expose at a h-line (405 nm wavelength) dose of 40 mJ/cm².
Immerse the wafer in a tray of CD-26 photoresist developer.
Gently agitate the solution for 1 min until the metal interconnects pattern has been fully developed.
Rinse in a tray of deionized water (DI) for 1 min and blow dry.
Thermally evaporate 3 nm of Cr followed by 80 nm of Au.

Immerse the wafer into a flat beaker of remover PG for approximately 3 hours until the metal has fully undercut, leaving the metal only in the desired interconnect and I/O pad regions of mesh electronics.
Rinse in isopropyl alcohol.
Blow dry.
Use PL mask-3 to define Pt electrodes.
Load the wafer into the mask aligner.
Expose the S1805 with PL mask-3 corresponding to the Pt electrodes at a h-line dose of 40 mJ/cm².
Immerse the wafer in a tray of CD-26 photoresist developer.
Gently agitate the solution for 1 minute until the Pt electrodes pattern has been fully developed.
Rinse in a tray of DI water for 1 minute.
Blow dry.
Use an electron beam evaporator to deposit 3 nm of Cr followed by 50 nm of Pt.
Immerse the wafer into a flat beaker of remover PG for approximately 3 hours until the metal has fully undercut, leaving Pt only at the desired electrode sites of mesh electronics.
Rinse in isopropyl alcohol.
Blow dry.
Use PL mask-4 to define the top passivating layer of mesh electronics with SU-8 negative photoresist.
Repeat steps 1.2.1 through 1.2.5, except exposing with PL mask-4 corresponding to the top passivating mesh layer of SU-8.
Hard bake the wafer on a hotplate at 190 °C for 1 hour.
Treat the wafer with oxygen plasma at 50 W for 1 min.
Combine hydrochloric acid, ferric chloride, and DI in a flat beaker at a volumetric ratio of 1:1:20 respectively to make a Ni etchant solution.
Immerse the wafer into the Ni etchant solution for approximately 3 h until the mesh electronics are released from the Si wafer.
Transfer the released mesh electronics probes from Ni etchant to a beaker of DI using a Pasteur pipette.
Rinse the mesh electronics by transferring them at least three times between fresh beakers of DI.
Disinfect the mesh electronics by transferring them to a 70%/30% ethanol/water solution.
Transfer the mesh electronics to sterile water for rinsing.
Seal the end opposite the circular screw fastener on the pipette holder with epoxy to prevent leakage during injection.
Let the epoxy harden before proceeding.
Insert a glass capillary needle into the pipette holder.
Fasten the glass capillary needle in place using the circular tightening screw and cone washer.
Attach a 1 mL syringe to the side outlet of the pipette holder using a 2–4 cm length of capillary tubing.
Insert the glass capillary needle into the 100-mL beaker of PBS containing the mesh electronics.
Position the end of the needle near the I/O pads of a mesh electronics probe.
Manually retract the syringe to draw a mesh electronics probe into the needle.
Push/pull the syringe plunger while still immersed in saline to adjust the position of mesh electronics within the needle.
Carefully detach the capillary tubing from the side outlet of the pipette holder.
Detach it slowly to avoid creating a suction force that could alter the position of the mesh electronics within the needle.
Anesthetize mice with a mixture of 75 mg/kg ketamine and 1 mg/kg dexdomitor.
Verify the degree of anesthesia using the toe pinch method.
Maintain body temperature at 37 °C during surgery by placing the mouse on a homeothermic blanket.
Autoclave all metal surgical instruments for 1 hour prior to use.
Use sterilized gloves throughout the procedure.
Sterilize plastic instruments with 70% ethanol before use.
Disinfect the depilated scalp skin with iodophor before incision.
Apply antibiotic ointment around the wound after surgery for survival surgeries.
Return the mouse to a cage equipped with a 37 °C heating pad post-surgery.
Provide buprenorphine analgesia via intraperitoneal injection at a dose of 0.05 mg/kg body weight every 12 hours for up to 72 hours following surgery.
Isolate mice from other animals following surgery.
Euthanize mice via intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital at a dose of 270 mg/kg body weight or via transcardial perfusion.
Anesthetize the mouse and fix it in a stereotaxic frame.
Apply ocular lubricant to the mouse's eyes.
Use a dental drill and stereotaxic frame to open a craniotomy at the desired coordinates on the skull.
Open a second craniotomy away from the injection site for the insertion of a stainless-steel grounding screw or wire.
Fix a clamping substrate to the skull with dental cement.
Cut an approximately 1-mm wide gap in the substrate.
Mount the pipette holder with the needle containing mesh electronics onto the stereotaxic frame using a right-angle end clamp.
Attach the side outlet of the pipette holder to a 5 mL syringe fastened in a syringe pump using an approximately 0.5–1 m length of capillary tubing.
Ensure there are no bubbles in the capillary tubing before connecting it to the pipette holder.
Use the stereotaxic frame to position the tip of the needle at the desired starting location within the brain.
Position the camera to display the top of the mesh electronics probe within the glass needle.
Initiate the flow by setting the syringe pump to a low speed and pressing Start.
Slowly increase the flow rate if the mesh electronics probe does not move within the needle.
Use the stereotaxic frame to guide the needle to the FFC clamping substrate.
Flow the solution with the syringe pump to generate slack in the mesh electronics interconnects.
Resume the flow at a fast rate to eject the mesh electronics I/O pads onto the clamping substrate.
Bend the I/O pads to a 90° angle as close to the first I/O pad as possible.
Dry the bent I/O pads in place with gently flowing compressed air.
Cut the clamping substrate at a straight edge approximately 0.5–1 mm from the edge of the I/O pads.
Cut off extraneous parts of the clamping substrate that will hinder insertion into the PCB-mounted 32-channel ZIF connector.
Insert I/O pads into ZIF connector on PCB.
Close latch to secure I/O pads.
Measure impedance between channels and ground screw.
Unlatch ZIF connector if impedance values are too high.
Adjust insertion of I/O pads and retest for successful connection.
Cover ZIF connector with dental cement for protection.
Cover exposed mesh electronics interconnects with dental cement.
Bend FFC at the gap in substrate to reduce mechanical strain.
Fix PCB onto mouse skull using cement.
Allow cement to harden to create a robust head-stage.
Place mouse in tailveiner or restrainer.
Insert preamplifier PCB into standard amplifier connector on head-stage PCB.
Ground reference screw with separate cable.
Leave mouse in restrainer for restrained recordings.
Record data using data acquisition system for desired time period.
Release mouse from restrainer after inserting preamplifier and grounding reference screw.
Record data while the mouse behaves freely.
Put the mouse back in the restrainer if necessary after the recording session.
Remove the grounding wire and preamplifier from the mouse.
Release the mouse back to its cage and return it to the animal facility until the next recording session.
Anesthetize the mouse at the desired time post-injection.
Transcardially perfuse the anesthetized mouse with formaldehyde.
Remove the brain tissue containing mesh electronics after perfusion.
Freeze and cryosection the removed brain into 10-µm thick slices.
Rinse the frozen brain tissue sections three times in 1x PBS.
Block the sections in a solution of 0.3% Triton X-100 and 5% goat serum in 1x PBS at room temperature for 1 hour.
Incubate the sections with primary antibody solutions including rabbit anti-NeuN, mouse anti-Neurofilament, and rat anti-GFAP overnight at 4 °C.
Rinse the sections nine times for a total of 40 minutes with 1x PBS.
Incubate the brain sections with secondary antibody solutions.
Rinse the sections 9 times for a total of 30 min with 1x PBS.
Mount the sections on glass slides with coverslips using antifade mountant.
Leave the slides in the dark for at least 24 h before imaging.
Image the slides with a confocal microscope using 488 nm, 561 nm, and 633 nm lasers.
Use differential interference contrast (DIC) to image the mesh electronics on the same microscope.
